title: Signal Tinderbox — Friction Diary and Micro‑Vignettes
content:
Purpose / framing:
This is a living tinderbox of short customer vignettes and synthesis sketches tied to runtime friction we keep seeing in the field (march — early april 2026). Goal is to capture small, repeatable patterns, propose low-effort probes, and give quick engineering impact context so product/eng can triage what to fold into micropatches vs larger workstreams.

Executive summary (tl;dr):
- Theme: customers repeatedly hit three operational pain modes — intermittent latency spikes on tail requests, unexpected KV cache invalidation patterns after prompt prefixing, and confusion about model variant fallbacks when Dedicated capacity is saturated.
- Short fixes available (<=2 engineer days): clearer console error surfacing for fallback events; quick prefix-preservation toggle in SDK (beta); small heuristics to keep KV cache warm for steady chat sessions.
- Medium work (2–6 wks): routing policy visibility in Console (why request routed to cheaper variant), deterministic canary rollback UX, and tracing augmentation to link token-level cost anomalies to route/model selection.

Representative micro‑vignettes (raw field notes):
1) "Healthcare workflow bot" (large enterprise, Dedicated): intermittent 200–400ms extra tail for long (3–5k token) summarization requests during peak hours. Customer observed latency correlated with autoscale events. They feared SLA breach. Partial workaround: lower batch window during peak.
   Notes: autoscale + prefix-KV miss combo. Possible short probe: emit autoscale-phase tag into trace and surface in Console latencymap.

2) "Legal review assistant" (mid-market): prompts that prepend dynamic case metadata (per-call) caused the prefix-KV hits — cache essentially invalidated and token cost doubled for some sessions. They wanted an explicit SDK option to mark stable vs ephemeral prefix text.
   Notes: obvious UX fix is a prefix stability flag. Engineering: a flag that separates prefix from ephemeral context in KV-key derivation. Low risk.

3) "Embedded chat (SaaS)" (AI-native startup): unexpected fallback to a quantized smaller model during short capacity blips; results were noticeably lower quality and customers opened CS tickets. They didn’t see any Console event indicating fallback.
   Notes: Add a visible fallback event (route_reason) with candidate variant list; tie to customer notifications and optional automated rollback config.

Synthesis of root causes we keep seeing:
- Observability gap: customers cannot tie quality or cost anomalies to routing/fallbacks; Console shows metrics but not the causal breadcrumb (route choice -> model variant -> autoscale phase -> KV state).
- KV cache semantics ambiguity: SDK/Docs don't surface how dynamic prompt prefixes affect cache keys. People assume prefixing is free.
- Autoscale-induced transient latency: during pod spin-up and placement, requests that hit cold KV/cache/comp action see spikes; this interacts poorly with continuous-batching heuristics.

Quick fixes and microprobes (low effort):
- Console: show "recent fallback events" card per customer for last 24h (status: small frontend + backend telemetry join).
- SDK: add optional prefix_stability enum {stable, ephemeral, session} which changes KV keying. Document with examples.
- Traces: attach autoscale_phase and chosen_variant as tags to traces emitted for 5xx/>=x latency.
- Run a 2‑week experiment enabling aggressive KV pre-warm for top 20% sessions (by token length) in staging with a couple customers. Measure tail latency and cost delta.

Engineering impact sketches (very rough):
- Fallback visibility: backend telemetry + console card -> ~1.5 engineer-weeks (1 backend + 1 frontend split) + small schema change for traces.
- Prefix flag: SDK changes (python/ts + docs + lightweight runtime support) -> 3–5 engineer-days.
- KV-warm experiment: orchestration + infra config -> 1–2 engineer-weeks.

Customer-facing framing / suggested copy for Console/Release notes:
- "New: Request fallback insights — see when Redwood drops to a compatible variant to preserve availability, and why. Enabled for Dedicated accounts by default (opt-out in settings)."
- "SDK: prefix_stability flag — mark parts of your prompt as stable to improve KV cache reuse and lower per‑token cost for long conversations."

Measurement & acceptance criteria for microfixes:
- Fallback card: pilot with 4 customers. Acceptance = customers can link at least one open support ticket to a displayed fallback event, and time to root cause < 1 business day (baseline unknown).
- Prefix flag: decrease KV-miss rate on annotated sessions by >=40% in pilot.
- KV-warm probe: reduce 95p tail latency on long requests by >=15% with <8% cost increase.

Open questions / risks to surface:
- Privacy/compliance: storing more KV‑warm metadata or prefix‑stability in telemetry — confirm PII boundaries for customer accounts (eng/security check required).
- Metrics noise: autoscale-phase tagging may add noise — how to ensure sampling is useful and not costly?
- Determinism: if SDK flag changes behavior, how to make rollout smooth for customers already trained on one pattern? Need migration doc and default conservative behavior.

Next actions (owners + rough ETA):
- Aisha G. (CS) -> recruit 3 pilot customers for prefix flag pilot (ETA: 1 week).
- Eng (observability) -> prototype fallback event surfacing and autoscale_phase trace tag (ETA: spike 2 weeks). JIRA ticket: JIRA-OPS-4107.
- Product -> draft Console copy and privacy checklist; coordinate with legal for telemetry scope (ETA: 1 week).

Notes-to-self / frictiony fragments worth keeping:
- customers sometimes paste entire doc as prefix every call (ugh). Could add a prompt-size warning in SDK.
- multiple tickets mention "sudden cheap model responses" — we should check policy that chooses fallback variants by cost/latency; maybe surface policy weights.
- keep short vid demo showing how prefix_stability reduces cost on a long chat (good for sales/training).

Appendix: raw snippets from tickets (anonymized):
- "We saw a drop in quality around 2026-03-09 14:21 UTC; no events in Console; user experienced hallucinations"
- "Our batch jobs spike token cost when the metadata prefix changes every run — is cache scope per-tenant or per-session?"
- "Why did my Dedicated route get a different model? We had a reserved pool..."

If helpful, I can turn this into a short one‑pager for Eng leadership or convert to a compact slate for the next oncall handoff. For now, keeping as living record in case patterns evolve.

— Noah P., CS (field)
